did_you_know.text: The chapter takes place during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, when Jeremiah receives the command to act concerning the Rechabites.
The LORD commands Jeremiah to bring the Rechabites into one of the chambers in the house of the LORD and offer them wine; this act is meant to serve as a tangible message to the people.

The Rechabites are brought to the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, who is called in the verse “a man of God,” near the chamber of the officials and close to the chamber of the doorkeeper.
The Rechabites refuse to drink wine because Jonadab son of Rechab, their ancestor, commanded them never to drink wine—themselves, their sons, or their daughters.

The way of life they were commanded to follow included refraining from building houses, sowing fields, and planting vineyards. They were to live in tents so that they might live long in the land where they resided.
The Rechabites explain that they moved to Jerusalem because of the armies of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the armies of Aram, but even there they continued to obey Jonadab’s command.
The LORD contrasts the Rechabites’ faithfulness to Jonadab’s commands with Judah’s behavior: the Rechabites obeyed their ancestor’s command, but the people did not obey the LORD’s words.
According to the chapter, the punishment of Judah and Jerusalem came because the people did not listen to the LORD’s calls, delivered through his prophets, to turn from their evil ways and serve him.

The house of the Rechabites is given the promise that a descendant of Jonadab son of Rechab will always stand before the LORD; this promise expresses the survival and continuity of the Rechabite family.
